v1.feedback: The conceptual morph is legit — Pollock's multi-swing chaos collapsed to a single ensō pivot, viscosity cranked, palette shifted to sumi-ink — but 102K additive-blended particles doing gentle orbits will likely read as a luminous soft disk rather than the sparse decisive marks shibumi demands. Kill 80-90% of particles or cluster them into distinct filament groups so individual brush-hair strokes emerge with negative space between them; the point sizes (0.3–0.8 base) are too uniform and small to differentiate mark from fog. The breath mechanic is poetic but nearly invisible at 0.3 amplitude — either commit to a visible gather-release that reshapes the silhouette or remove the compute.

v2.feedback: The ensō-pivot concept is a smart shibumi reading of the Pollock parent — collapsing many chaotic swings into one deliberate circular gesture — and the heavy attractor damping plus viscosity correctly morph the parent rather than replacing it. However, 7 concentric filament orbits around a drifting center likely read as a generic orbital swirl rather than a recognizable calligraphic form; collapse to 2–3 filaments with more varied stroke weight so individual marks are legible in 2s. The breath mechanic is conceptually strong but the inhale/exhale force magnitudes (0.8 / 1.2) compete with the orbital tension, risking a pulsing blob; tie breathForce to a slow envelope that spends more time exhaled (asymmetric duty cycle) so the silhouette holds shape longer. The dp.y -= 0.04 gravity drags the whole composition downward over time without a compensating recentering — either remove it or add a very slow y-drift correction to keep the form centered in frame.
